Finland has monitored nutrition for a long time
In Finland, the nutrition of the adult population has been regularly monitored in the
national  FinDiet  Surveys  since  1982.  This  representative  population  data  form  the
basis  of  nutrition  monitoring  by  providing  evidence-based  information  concerning
Finnish adults’ food consumption, nutrient intakes, sources of intake, use of dietary
supplements and changes over time. People’s nutritional status is also evaluated using
blood and urine samples. Nutrition monitoring provides information that is necessary
to identify nutritional risk groups in the population. The information is also required
to assess the risks posed by food contaminants and the environmental impact of diets.
The data also enable scientific research and participation in global nutrition monitoring
projects. Extending the regular nutrition monitoring carried out by the Finnish Institute
for Health and Welfare to children, young people, pregnant and lactating women, and
older people is an important national goal.
